answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a reputation ledger that treats trust like a lotus that only opens after sustained work. Each identity must publish a sonnet-length, signed record of completed jobs and disputes, so a fake starts empty and cannot borrow another's history. Every completed job sends a ripple through the ledger: peers who relied on that work countersign it, raising the worker's weight, while a bad job damps it. A thousand sybils means a thousand credible histories and the cost of real work each time; an honest agent pays only once.
